problem.text: Define the sum of a finite set of integers to be the sum of the elements of the set. Let $D$ be the set of positive divisors of $700$. How many nonempty subsets of $D$ have an even sum? (Simplify as reasonably as possible)

steps.title: Where to start: only the odd elements matter for parity
steps.body: The question is about whether a sum is even. Even numbers never change the parity of a sum, so what matters is how many odd numbers the subset contains. That means we should sort the divisors of $700$ into odd and even ones. First factor: $700 = 2^2\cdot 5^2\cdot 7$.

your_turn.prompt: How many positive divisors does $700$ have?
your_turn.answer: $18$: a divisor is $2^a 5^b 7^c$ with $3$ choices for $a$, $3$ for $b$ and $2$ for $c$, and $3\cdot 3\cdot 2 = 18$.

steps.title: Split the divisors into odd and even
steps.body: A divisor is odd exactly when it has no factor of $2$, so the odd divisors are the divisors of $5^2\cdot 7$. There are $3\cdot 2 = 6$ of them. Every other divisor is even.

your_turn.prompt: How many even divisors does $700$ have, and why?
your_turn.answer: $12$: the exponent of $2$ is $1$ or $2$ ($2$ choices), times the $6$ divisors of $5^2\cdot 7$. Equivalently, $18 - 6 = 12$.

steps.title: Count subsets with an even number of odd divisors
steps.body: A subset has an even sum exactly when it contains an even number of odd divisors: $0$, $2$, $4$ or $6$ of them. The $12$ even divisors can be included or left out freely, giving $2^{12}$ choices. Careful: the empty subset (no odd and no even divisors) has sum $0$, which is even, so it gets counted here even though the problem excludes it.

your_turn.prompt: In how many ways can we pick an even number of the $6$ odd divisors?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
Multiplying the independent choices gives $2^{12}\cdot 2^5 = 2^{17} = 131072$ subsets with an even sum, including the empty set. Removing the empty set,
$$2^{17} - 1 = 131071.$$ The answer is **$131071$**.
